rows.claim: C >= g(A) > 1.163 for the explicit far-block set A of #5's certificate script at L = 100000 (|A| = 101478), rebuilt here from its stated rule
rows.where: #5 there4iam, 2026-07-31 (materials.zip, 3_CERTIFICATE.py read as text; Penman--Wells 2013 give 1.12594, the repository 1.12194)
rows.how: |A+A| = 1,200,837 and |A-A| = 848,817 by exact bitset sumsets; g > 1163/1000 decided as the integer inequality |A+A|^1000 |A|^163 > |A-A|^1163

rows.claim: the explicit 23,646-integer set of #5 §5 violates |A+A| + |A| <= |A-A| + diam(A) + 1 (the strong form of its own conjecture), by 89
C >= 1.6269 by the "hollow bridge" instance of #5 (43 gadgets, an 86-digit modulus)
rows.how: the set is not enumerable (modulus ~10^86); its count rests on the write-up's own argument, which is machine-generated and unreviewed by its authors' statement; nothing finite to decide here
rows.note: C = 2 itself is now a theorem: Lin--Li, arXiv:2607.27199 (29 Jul 2026), which #5's author acknowledges in the thread; cited, not decided here

rows.claim: a 3-D moving sofa of volume >= 1.8558404 (#8; the repository records >= 1.81)
rows.how: the certificate is a floating-point cube count under stated position and angle tolerances (0.005, 0.05 degrees; the author's own note: 1.7701 at the quick-start tolerances); no exact object is published. To decide it an interval instrument would have to enclose every pose, prove the swept region contains each counted cube and sum a rational lower bound — not built here
rows.note: the repository's own pipeline (JAX, GPU) is what was run; a measurement, not a certificate
